facts.statement: Californosaurus is an extinct genus of marine reptile known from fossils in California and Germany.
facts.quote: Californosaurus ('California lizard') is an extinct genus of ichthyosaur, an extinct marine reptile, from the Lower Hosselkus Limestone (Carnian, Late Triassic) of California, and also the Muschelkalk (Ladinian, Middle Triassic) of Germany.

facts.statement: John Campbell Merriam described the species in 1902 as Shastasaurus perrini, honoring discoverer James Perrin Smith.
facts.quote: John Campbell Merriam (1902) described it as a new species of Shastasaurus, S. perrini, honouring Professor James Perrin Smith as discoverer, based on holotype UCMP 9119.

facts.statement: Oscar Kuhn established the genus name Californosaurus in 1934 because the previous name Delphinosaurus was already used for a different animal.
facts.quote: However, Delphinosaurus had in 1853 by Eichwald been previously used for an ophthalmosaurid from Albian-Cenomanian deposits in European Russia, Delphinosaurus kiprijanoffii, and Oscar Kuhn (1934) provided the generic replacement name Californosaurus.

facts.statement: Californosaurus had a long-snouted head that was small relative to its body, similar to primitive ichthyosaurs.
facts.quote: The long-snouted head is small in comparison with the rest of the body, as in basal ichthyosaurs such as Mixosaurus and Cymbospondylus.

facts.statement: Its tail was sharply angled downward with a small vertical fluke, a trait shared with more advanced ichthyosaurs.
facts.quote: The tail is sharply turned downwards, in common with more advanced ichthyosaurs, with a small vertical fluke.

facts.statement: Fossil evidence suggests Californosaurus may have possessed a small dorsal fin.
facts.quote: It may have had a small dorsal fin.

facts.statement: The animal had between 45 and 50 vertebrae before the sacrum.
facts.quote: There is a small number of pre-sacral vertebrae (45 or 50).

facts.statement: Its flipper bones were circular and widely spaced, creating a round appearance for the flippers.
facts.quote: The phalanges (digit bones) are circular and widely spaced, giving the flipper a round appearance.

facts.statement: Californosaurus was a medium-sized ichthyosaur reaching lengths of up to 3 meters.
facts.quote: It was a medium-sized ichthyosaur, measuring up to 3 m long.

facts.statement: Californosaurus fed on fish and other small marine animals.
facts.quote: It fed on fish and other small marine creatures.

facts.statement: Like other ichthyosaurs, it likely never left the water and gave birth in the sea.
facts.quote: Like other ichthyosaurs it probably never ventured onto dry land, and gave birth in the water.

facts.statement: Fossils are found in the Carnian stage of the Late Triassic in California and the Ladinian stage of the Middle Triassic in Germany.
facts.quote: from the Lower Hosselkus Limestone (Carnian, Late Triassic) of California, and also the Muschelkalk (Ladinian, Middle Triassic) of Germany.

facts.statement: The genus lived during the Carnian age between 237 and 227.3 million years ago.
facts.quote: Time range: Carnian to Carnian (237 to 227.3 million years ago)

facts.statement: Californosaurus belongs to the suborder Shastasauria.
It is considered one of the most basal true ichthyosaurs known.
facts.quote: Es uno de los ictiosaurios verdaderos (Euichthyosauria) más basales que se conocen.
